text:
matt_l: Quick follow-up from today's all-hands — small thread to clarify kernel priorities. We talked about landing the new fast-path kernels vs. continuing batching/kv-cache improvements. Can we get a concrete sequence and short timeline? Also flagging possible perf regressions observed in canary.

anya_r: Good call, matt. Short version: fast-path kernels are highest priority for p99 latency targets; batching/kv-cache is parallel work for throughput/cost. Plan: fast-path experimental patch next week, canary the week after, batching changes start in 3 wks. I'll post PRs and the rollout plan.

davidc: adding detail: the fast-path PR touches attention kernel and kernel selector. Early microbench shows 8-12% p99 improvement for short seqs but +4% alloc during warmup. We need a short prewarm script in canary to avoid warmup regressions.

karen_w: from product: which customers will see p99 wins first? Any risk to Dedicated customers with reserved capacity? we should scope canary to hosted first.

anya_r: Agree — hosted only for initial canary. We'll keep Dedicated on the current kernel and provide a toggle for on-prem/private. No SLA changes.

matt_l: @davidc can you share the prewarm snippet we should run in canary? Also, who owns rollback if canary shows higher error rate?

davidc: snippet below (will paste to ops channel too):

```
# prewarm: run short generation to populate kv cache
for i in range(50):
    call_api({"prompt":"prewarm step %d"%i, "max_tokens":4})
```

Owner for rollback: eng-sre (karen_w will coordinate with infra).

infra-bot: Canary scheduled: hosted/fast-path-v1 -> start 2026-05-12T15:00Z, duration 48h. Rollback window 4h after anomalies. Watchers: @davidc @anya_r @karen_w.

karen_w: I'll open a customer-impact note and ping support to watch for latency/error trends. If we see >5% p99 regression or errors >0.2% we abort.

matt_l: Thanks — please add the canary dashboard link when ready. :thumbsup:
